narration: The framework takes synchronized multimodal inputs consisting of RGB video frames capturing human motion and pressure sensor mat recordings capturing ground interaction over time.
Each input modality is processed through dedicated encoders followed by Local Spatio-temporal Attention Modules to extract enriched temporal feature representations.
Extracted visual and pressure features are integrated by the Fusion Cross-Attention Module, which feeds the fused multimodal representations into a regressor.

The regressor estimates body pose theta and global translation T to recover 3D joint locations J(theta, T) and 2D orthographic projections, supervised by corresponding pose, translation, 3D, and 2D losses.
The predicted 3D human meshes reconstruct continuous motion on the ground plane, guided by a contact loss with detailed body contact region modeling.

Finally, the internal architecture of the Fusion Cross-Attention Module is detailed below, employing pressure queries with image keys and values, followed by feed-forward layers and residual connections.
